A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 16-page ELiC paper, including supplementary Sections A-H. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical substantive content; only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp differs.

before.justification: v2 reports original ELiC compression, runtime and ablation results on Ford and SemanticKITTI in Section 5, with additional empirical analyses in supplementary Sections D-H.

after.justification: v3 retains these original compression, runtime, ablation and supplementary results, including Tables 1-5 and S1-S3.

M1.justification: The Morton hierarchy, cross-bit-depth feature propagation, BoE selection, training objective and encoding/decoding procedures are identical, including supplementary Section E's asynchronous encoding.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ford and SemanticKITTI for the same LiDAR geometry compression task. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain G-PCCv30, RENO, RENO-Large, Unicorn and TopNet. Draco also remains in Figure S5; ablation comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains identical data splits, quantization, 12-16-bit evaluation, BPP/D1/D2 metrics, training budgets and runtime procedures. Supplementary experimental settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The feature-propagation, BoE pool-size and Morton-order ablations are identical. Supplementary asynchronous-encoding, parameter-efficiency and bit-allocation analyses are also retained without revision.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Both report the same averages without seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative observations are unchanged throughout the main paper and supplement. For example, Table 1 retains ELiC's mean encoding/decoding times of 0.121/0.111 seconds.

T1.justification: Equations 1-20 and their mathematical reasoning are identical, including the Morton-order coordinate transformations and preservation argument in supplementary Section C.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same three methodological contributions and claims about compression efficiency and real-time throughput on Ford and SemanticKITTI.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and limitations are unchanged, including the fixed 4+4 factorization limitation and supplementary discussion of training favoring higher bit-depth levels.

D1.justification: Software, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing and implementation disclosures are identical. The code/pretrained-model access statement and supplementary morton.py reference are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, all 42 references and ELiC's positioning as an extension of RENO are identical.

P1.justification: Only the first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv:2511.14070v2, dated 19 Mar 2026, to v3, dated 30 Apr 2026. All paper prose, headings and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2-16 render identically; first-page visual differences are confined to the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: v3 only updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations and supplementary material are identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
